comparisons.peer_summary: The 2023 Plan permits nonstatutory and incentive stock options with exercise prices not less than 100% of fair market value at grant, payable in full at exercise. Generally, these options vest over four years and expire within seven years.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose the specific terms governing the exercise price of stock options under their respective primary equity plans. AVGO’s 2007 Plan requires that stock options and SARs have an exercise price no less than the fair market value on the date of grant. Similarly, AMD’s 2023 Plan mandates that the exercise price for nonstatutory and incentive stock options cannot be less than 100% of the fair market value on the date of the grant, reflecting a consistent industry standard for option pricing floors.

sentences.text: Under the 2007 Plan, we may grant stock options and stock appreciation rights with an exercise price that is no less than the fair market value on the date of grant, restricted stock, RSUs, and other stock-based or cash-based awards to employees.

The exercise price of the shares subject to each nonstatutory stock option and incentive stock option cannot be less than 100% of the fair market value of the Company's common stock on the date of the grant.
